business.title: Vibration characteristics of a tracked combine harvester chassis frame during progressive component engagement and field operation
business.desc: The chassis frame of a tracked combine harvester is subjected to periodic excitation from the engine and working components together with random excitation from the crawler–ground interaction. This study combined a stationary progressive-superposition test with a supplementary field-operational test to compare changes associated with component engagement and describe vibration during field operation. In the stationary test, triaxial accelerations were measured at four excitation-source supports and four chassis-frame locations under six working conditions. Root mean square (RMS), fast Fourier transform (FFT), and short-time Fourier transform (STFT) analyses identified vibration intensity, dominant frequencies, and energy evolution. Engagement of the threshing and cleaning system increased the three-axis averaged RMS acceleration at monitoring point 6 from 4.02 to 15.21 m/s2 and increased the amplitudes of components near 157–158 Hz at several monitoring points. In the field test, all working components and the traveling system operated simultaneously, with a triaxial accelerometer mounted on the outer face of the crawler beam at monitoring point 6. After conversion to the machine coordinate system, the longitudinal, lateral, and vertical RMS accelerations were 2.44, 3.92, and 6.37 m/s2, respectively. The vertical direction was dominant, with major power spectral density peaks at 15.63 and 31.25 Hz. The stationary tests show how vibration changed as components were engaged. The single field measurement characterizes the combined response at the crawler beam during harvesting.

technology.title: Estimation of renewable energy consumption and its determinants for OECD countries using biased estimators
technology.desc: Renewable energy consumption is influenced by factors, including trade dynamics, foreign direct investment, labor market conditions, industrial development, fossil fuel dependence, and population structure. Therefore, this study is modeled by a linear regression model for renewable energy consumption in OECD countries. The model utilizes several determinants of renewable energy consumption, including exports, foreign direct investment, labor force, industrialization, fossil fuel energy consumption, life expectancy, carbon dioxide emissions, imports, gross domestic product per capita and urban population. Data from 2021 regarding these variables are analyzed for 38 OECD countries. However, the model established for OECD countries has a multicollinearity problem, making it unstable with classical estimators. Biased estimators must be used for model estimation. Accordingly, Ordinary Least Square (OLS), Ridge and Generalized Maximum Entropy (GME) estimators are used, and the estimators are compared according to the Mean Squared Error criterion. In this study, we obtained that increases in exports, industrialization, fossil fuel energy consumption, and urban population lead to an increase in renewable energy consumption, whereas increases in carbon dioxide emissions, imports, and life expectancy at birth lead to a decrease in renewable energy consumption. Although some of the results may initially appear surprising, they stem from the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic (e.g., exports, urban population, carbon dioxide emissions, life expectancy at birth, etc.). Furthermore, findings for study show that the superiority of using the GME as a biased estimator in the presence of a multicollinearity problem. Therefore, for future research, the use of biased estimators—and the GME in particular—is recommended in situations where model assumptions are not met.
